title: Find Good Days to Rob the Bank
summary: Given a 0-indexed integer array security, where security[i] represents the number of guards on duty on the i^th day, and an integer time, identify all days i where the number of guards is non-increasing for the preceding time days and non-decreasing for the following time days.
statement: Given a 0-indexed integer array security, where security[i] represents the number of guards on duty on the i^th day, and an integer time, identify all days i where the number of guards is non-increasing for the preceding time days and non-decreasing for the following time days. Specifically, day i is a good day to rob the bank if: - security[i - time] is greater than or equal to security[i - time + 1], and so on, up to security[i]. - security[i] is less than or equal to security[i + 1], and so on, up to security[i + time - 1]. Return a list of all such good days, in any order.
constraints: A day is good when the preceding time transitions are nonincreasing and the following time transitions are nondecreasing.
Day indices must have time available days on both sides.
Return all good indices in increasing order.
hints: Precompute how many consecutive qualifying transitions end and begin at every day.
Scan left-to-right for nonincreasing run lengths and right-to-left for nondecreasing run lengths.
Index i qualifies when before[i]>=time and after[i]>=time.
Those two run lengths are exactly the required inequalities on each side, and the threshold also excludes boundary-short indices.
editorial: Those two run lengths are exactly the required inequalities on each side, and the threshold also excludes boundary-short indices.

tests.explanation: Days two and three each have two nonincreasing steps before and two nondecreasing steps after.
With no required neighboring days, every index qualifies.
